newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ANGRY FANS FIREBOMB FLAMENGO HEADQUARTERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY FANS FIREBOMB FLAMENGO HEADQUARTERS.

text.p: A meeting room at beleaguered Rio soccer club Flamengo was firebombed on Tuesday and a group of angry fans claimed responsibility.

Witnesses said about six men ran past the room just after a directors' meeting had finished on Monday night, threw a bottle full of inflammable liquid on to the floor and then set fire to it before fleeing.
Some windows were smashed and curtains were set on fire but damage appeared to be minimal.
"We are a group of 15 people. We used a drinks bottle with petrol," a telephone caller later told a local radio station.
"We didn't achieve our objective but this isn't the end of it. We are Flamengo fans disgusted with the mistakes made by the directors."
Club president Kleber Leite, who was in Sao Paulo at the time, blamed his enemies for the act.
"The real perpetrators of this act are not the ones who threw petrol and set fire to it," he said. "They are the people who hide in the opposition and want to destabilise the club."
Vice-president Michel Assef, surveying the scene, said: "I can't believe this is the work of Flamengo supporters."
Leite, who took over as president at the start of 1995, has faced increasing opposition among fans as his incessant wheeling and dealing has failed to produce a decent team.
The club, which claims to be the best supported in the country, are currently 22nd in the 26-team championship.
Leite began his reign in spectacular style by signing Brazilian World Cup hero Romario in early 1995 but since then his signings have been criticised as increasingly incoherent.
More than 50 players have been bought and sold in the Leite era and he has employed six coaches.
During one three-month period last year, Flamengo signed former international Bebeto, sold Romario to Spanish club Valencia, resold Bebeto and brought Romario back on loan.
The latest storm has blown up this week following reports that Leite wanted to replace coach Sebastiao Rocha with Paulo Autuori from Cruzeiro.

Although Flamengo have not officially announced the change, Cruzeiro president Zeze Pereira accused the club of being unethical in approaching Autuori while at Flamengo there was criticism at yet another change.
"Once again it will be Flamengo who lose out," said Romario, who has rejoined Valencia but made a flying visit to the club on Monday. "Big uncle (Rocha's nickname) is not to blame for the results."
Rocha himself said: "I will find another path for my life."
Flamengo have not scored a goal in the championship since Romario's loan from Valencia expired last month.
